metadata.name: Mini-PFN: two bear-survival worlds
metadata.purpose: A real trained educational model with a deliberately tiny known task prior.
metadata.training_curve_metric: Observed log loss on the same 2,048 independent validation tasks at each checkpoint.
metadata.selection: Fixed training schedule; final weights used. No selection against test results.
metadata.prior: One world A or B drawn with equal probability per task. Independent balanced binary bear/strategy features. World A survival probability logistic(1) when B=L and logistic(-1) otherwise; world B reverses these. Outcomes independently sampled conditional on the shared world and row features.
metadata.inputs: Raw 0/1 context columns B,L,Y; raw 0/1 query B,L. No world identity, match indicator, posterior, or analytic Bayes output enters the model or its loss target.
metadata.training_target: One independently sampled Bernoulli query outcome per task; mean binary cross entropy.
metadata.architecture: Context MLP 3→32→32 and query MLP 2→32→32 with ReLU; separate linear Q,K,V maps; one scaled-dot-product cross-attention head; concatenate query representation and weighted value mixture; decoder MLP 64→32→1 with ReLU, then sigmoid.
limitations: This is not TabPFN and has not been evaluated on general tabular datasets.
It learns a deliberately restricted two-world prior with exactly four context rows and two binary features; it has no irrelevant-feature experiment.
Attention weights describe this trained computation, not feature importance, causal effects, or posterior world probabilities.
The analytic Bayesian comparison is exact for the specified prior; the neural approximation can differ.
Displayed context examples are selected illustrations, while aggregate performance uses an independent set of sampled tasks.
